subject: Maths
title: Year 9 Maths Exam 6
intro: You must not use a calculator. Show your working in the working box: method marks are given even when the final answer is wrong. "Show that" means write every step to reach the given answer. "Prove" means use algebra, not just numbers.

questions.q: A number line has a filled circle at −3 and an arrow going to the right. Which inequality does it show?
questions.ms: B1: x ≥ −3. Filled circle means −3 is included (≥); arrow to the right means bigger numbers.

questions.q: Expand 3x(2x − 5).
questions.ms: B1: 6x² − 15x. Multiply 3x by both terms: 3x × 2x = 6x², 3x × −5 = −15x.

questions.q: Factorise x2 + 2x − 24.
x is an integer. List all the values of x such that −7 < 3x + 2 ≤ 14.
questions.hint: Type the values from smallest to largest, separated by commas, like -2,0,3
questions.ms: Answer: −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. M1 for −9 < 3x ≤ 12. M1 for −3 < x ≤ 4. A1 for the full list (−3 is not included, 4 is included).

questions.q:
A van can carry a load of at most 900 kg. The driver weighs 85 kg and there are already 4 crates in the van, each weighing 120 kg.
Boxes weighing 45 kg each are added. Write an inequality and solve it to find the greatest number of boxes that can be added.
questions.ms: Answer: 7 boxes. M1 for 85 + 480 + 45b ≤ 900 (or 565 + 45b ≤ 900). M1 for 45b ≤ 335 so b ≤ 7.4… A1 for 7 (8 boxes would give 925 kg, which is too much).

questions.q:
Sara has n coins. Kareem has 4 times as many coins as Sara, but he then spends 45 of them. Kareem still has more coins than Sara.
Write down an inequality in terms of n to show this information.
questions.ms: Answer: 4n − 45 > n. B1 (must be >, not ≥).

questions.q: Use your inequality to find the least number of coins that Sara could have.
questions.ms: Answer: 16. M1 for 3n > 45 or n > 15. A1 for 16 (n must be a whole number greater than 15, so 15 is not allowed: 4 × 15 − 45 = 15, which is not more than 15).

questions.q:
Zayd chooses an integer. He divides it by 3 and then adds 12. His answer is less than 30.
What is the largest integer Zayd could have chosen?
questions.ms: Answer: 53. M1 for n ÷ 3 + 12 < 30. M1 for n ÷ 3 < 18, so n < 54. A1 for 53 (54 gives exactly 30, which is not less than 30).

questions.q: Expand and simplify (x − 1)(x + 5)(x − 3).
questions.ms: Answer: x³ + x² − 17x + 15. M1 for expanding two brackets, e.g. (x − 1)(x + 5) = x² + 4x − 5. M1 for multiplying by the third bracket with at least 4 correct terms out of 6 (x³ − 3x² + 4x² − 12x − 5x + 15). A1 cao.

questions.q: Factorise 3x2 − 13x − 10.
questions.ms: Answer: (3x + 2)(x − 5). M1 for splitting the middle term: 3x² − 15x + 2x − 10, or brackets that give two of the three terms. A1. Check: a × c = −30, and −15 × 2 = −30, −15 + 2 = −13.

questions.q: Factorise 4x2 + 4x − 15.
questions.ms: Answer: (2x − 3)(2x + 5). M1 for 4x² + 10x − 6x − 15, or brackets that give two of the three terms. A1. Check: a × c = −60, and 10 × −6 = −60, 10 + (−6) = 4.

questions.q: Factorise fully 2x2 − 98.
questions.ms: Answer: 2(x − 7)(x + 7). M1 for 2(x² − 49). A1 for the difference of two squares step. Common mistake: stopping at 2(x² − 49).

questions.q: Solve 5x2 − 13x − 6 = 0 by factorising.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 1/2,-3
questions.ms: Answer: x = 3 or x = −2/5. M1 for 5x² − 15x + 2x − 6 or (5x + 2)(x − 3). M1 for setting each bracket to 0. A1 for both answers (accept −0.4).

questions.q:
Nadia is solving x(x + 4) = 5x.
She divides both sides by x and gets x + 4 = 5, so x = 1.
Explain what Nadia has done wrong.
questions.ms: B1: dividing by x loses the solution x = 0. When x = 0, you would be dividing by zero, which is not allowed.

questions.q: Solve x(x + 4) = 5x correctly. Give all the solutions.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = 0 or x = 1. M1 for x² + 4x − 5x = 0, so x² − x = 0, or x(x − 1) = 0. A1 for both.

questions.q:
The curve y = (x + 5)(x − 3) is drawn.
Write down the x-coordinates where the curve crosses the x-axis.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = −5 and x = 3. M1 for setting each bracket to 0. A1 for both (watch the signs: x + 5 = 0 gives x = −5).

questions.q: Find the y-coordinate where the curve crosses the y-axis.
Find the coordinates of the turning point of the curve.
questions.ms: Answer: (−1, −16). M1 for x = −1 (halfway between −5 and 3). A1 for y = (4)(−4) = −16.

questions.q:
A ball is thrown upwards. Its height, h metres, after t seconds is h = 40t − 5t2.
After how many seconds does the ball land back on the ground?
questions.ms: Answer: 8 seconds. M1 for 5t(8 − t) = 0 or 40t − 5t² = 0. A1 for t = 8 (t = 0 is when it is thrown).

questions.q: Find the maximum height of the ball. (m)
questions.ms: Answer: 80 m. M1 for t = 4 (halfway between 0 and 8). A1 for h = 160 − 80 = 80.

questions.q: For how many seconds is the ball at least 60 m above the ground? (seconds)
questions.ms: Answer: 4 seconds. M1 for 40t − 5t² = 60 rearranged to t² − 8t + 12 = 0. M1 for (t − 2)(t − 6) = 0, so t = 2 and t = 6. A1 for 6 − 2 = 4 seconds.

questions.q:
A rectangle has length (2x + 1) cm and width (x − 2) cm. Its area is 25 cm2.
Show that 2x2 − 3x − 27 = 0.
questions.ms: M1 for (2x + 1)(x − 2) = 25. A1 for expanding to 2x² − 4x + x − 2 = 25, then 2x² − 3x − 27 = 0 (every step shown).

questions.q: Solve 2x2 − 3x − 27 = 0 and use your answer to find the perimeter of the rectangle. (cm)
questions.ms: Answer: 25 cm. M1 for (2x − 9)(x + 3) = 0. A1 for x = 4.5 (reject x = −3 because the width x − 2 would be negative). A1 for length 10 cm, width 2.5 cm, so perimeter 2 × (10 + 2.5) = 25 cm.

questions.q: Solve x2 + 2x − 15 > 0
questions.ms: Answer: x  3. M1 for (x + 5)(x − 3). M1 for critical values −5 and 3. A1 for x  3 (a U-shaped curve is above the x-axis outside its roots).

questions.q: Prove that (n + 5)2 − (n + 1)2 is always a multiple of 8 for every integer n.
questions.ms: M1 for expanding one bracket correctly: n² + 10n + 25 or n² + 2n + 1. M1 for 8n + 24. A1 for 8(n + 3) with a statement that this is a multiple of 8. Numerical examples only: 0 marks.

questions.q: Prove that the product of any two consecutive even numbers is always a multiple of 8.
questions.ms: M1 for 2n and 2n + 2 (any even number can be written 2n). M1 for 2n(2n + 2) = 4n² + 4n = 4n(n + 1). A1 for explaining that n and n + 1 are consecutive, so one of them is even, so n(n + 1) is even and 4 × an even number is a multiple of 8.
